questions.q: What does a write (state-changing) transaction need that a read call doesn't?
options: A paid subscription to the node provider
A faster internet connection than reads require
A second RPC endpoint dedicated to writes
Something that can sign — a private key, held by a Wallet or an account
questions.explain: Reads only need a connection to a node; writes must be signed by a private key before they can be broadcast, which is why Etherscan gates Write Contract behind Connect Wallet.

questions.q: In ethers.js v6, what object lets your code sign and send a transaction?
options: The ABI array alone
A Wallet built from a private key and a provider
An Interface object
A plain JsonRpcProvider with no additional setup
questions.explain: ethers.Wallet(PRIVATE_KEY, provider) is the signer — a Provider alone can only read, never sign.

questions.q: In viem, what does simulateContract do before you actually call writeContract?
options: Dry-runs the call to catch a revert before you spend any real gas
Switches your wallet client to a different chain
Automatically doubles your gas limit for safety
Permanently deploys a test copy of the contract
questions.explain: simulateContract performs a read-only dry run of the write, surfacing a revert reason up front instead of after you've paid for a failed transaction.

questions.q: Why does `tx.wait()` (ethers) or `waitForTransactionReceipt` (viem) matter after sending a transaction?
options: Because it's required to pay the gas fee
Because sendTransaction never actually submits anything until wait() is called
Because it cancels the transaction if called too late
Because sending a transaction only broadcasts it — the receipt tells you whether it was actually mined and succeeded
questions.explain: A resolved sendTransaction call just means the transaction was broadcast; waiting for the receipt confirms it was mined and tells you its real status.

questions.q: What real, concrete fields does a mined transaction's receipt expose, as seen on Etherscan's transaction detail page?
options: Status, gas used, the nonce it consumed, and EIP-1559 fee fields like base/max/max priority
The sender's full private key for verification
Only the transaction hash, nothing else
A list of every other pending transaction in the mempool
questions.explain: A receipt includes status, gas usage, nonce, and (for EIP-1559 transactions) the base fee, max fee, and max priority fee actually paid.
